Industry 4.0 is the fourth wave of technological advancement, introducing new digital technologies that transform industrial production.
Smart manufacturing integrates manufacturing assets with sensors, computing platforms, communication technology, data-intensive modeling, control, simulation, and predictive engineering.
The digital thread in smart manufacturing encompasses design, manufacturing, and product support operations driven by a digital flow of technical data and information.
Cyber threats to smart manufacturing can be motivated by espionage, financial gain, or other reasons to compromise data confidentiality, integrity, and availability.
NIST has established the Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) to help manufacturing entities enhance the security of their infrastructure.
Additive Layer Manufacturing (ALM) faces the challenge of intellectual property protection when outsourcing production, which can increase the attack surface.
Cloud manufacturing aims to enable full sharing, circulation, high utilization, and on-demand use of various manufacturing resources and capabilities.
Health-CPS is a cyber-physical system for patient-centric healthcare applications and services, built on cloud and big data analytics technologies.
Remote attestation is a key mechanism to verify the integrity of a system's software configuration and detect unintended or malicious modifications.
Hierarchical privacy preservation mechanisms are proposed to ensure the security of sensitive data in cloud manufacturing and health-CPS applications.
